answer: Clone keys can fill many grader seats and cash rewards before a rater isolates them. Each enrollee posts a jade bond of 17.4 units for 10 days in an umber sleeve, then plants 5 beacons at minutes 5, 16, 27, 39 and 51 of a 60-minute knoll circuit. Each beacon is a 44-bit commit checked by 6 neighbors on a 2304-cell mesh; two keys may share at most 0 cells. One seat costs 17.4; a 36-key farm needs 36 sleeves and 626.4 locked. A beacon over 65s late slashes 44% of the bond to those neighbors; a shared-cell hit burns both sleeves 100% and closes that knoll gate 78h; a reused commit is dropped.
